doc.citation: Wellman, C.H., Steemans, P. & Miller, M.A. (2015). Spore assemblages from Upper Ordovician and lowermost Silurian sediments recovered from the Qusaiba-1 shallow core hole, Qasim region, central Saudi Arabia. Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology 212, 111–126.
doc.comment: Table 2 contains 37 Ordovician samples and 293 taxon presences. Captions add nine occurrences to these samples and cite three unlisted depths, retained separately as unresolved records rather than confirmed additional samples. Table 2 prints depths in m, whereas Fig. 3 and captions use ft; neither has been silently corrected. Section 5 attributes assemblages to Qalibah, although Table 2 lists only Sarah and Qasim; that unresolved formation-level report is recorded separately without transferring table taxa to it. Earlier reports of this material include Steemans et al. (2008), Wellman et al. (2008), and Steemans et al. (2009), Origin and radiation of the earliest vascular land plants. Reworking is demonstrated for marine palynomorphs in glacial deposits, not individual spore occurrences. All assemblages are marine-dominated; cryptospores dominate the spores, and naturally separating hilate/trilete spores comprise less than 1% overall. Illustrated flags identify specimens explicitly captioned from the corresponding depth. Table spellings and abbreviations are retained, including Dyadospora., Sphaerosaccus and I. vavrdovae; Sphaerasaccus is used elsewhere in the paper. The oldest Qasim age is described inconsistently as not younger than early Katian (§2) or mid-Katian (§6.1); the sample boundary between its two chitinozoan zones is unspecified.

items.palaeogeo_unit_reported: western margin of the continent Gondwana
items.age_basis_detail: Graptolites and palynology (§§2,6.1). Chitinozoans suggest possibly an early Rhuddanian condensed section at 257–254.5 ft followed by a mid-Aeronian interval at 254.5–231 ft; these are geological intervals, not specified spore-sample depths.
items.notes: Unresolved formation attribution: §5 explicitly states that spore assemblages recovered throughout the Qalibah Formation are essentially identical and refers to Table 2, which actually lists only Sarah and Qasim samples. The narrative reports cryptospores, hilate spores and trilete spores, but provides no independently resolvable Qalibah sample list. No Table 2 taxon occurrences have been transferred to this record.
